course_outcomes.description: Understand core database concepts, relational data models, and ER schema design.
Formulate complex relational algebra expressions and advanced SQL queries.
Apply relational database design theory, functional dependencies, and normal forms (1NF to BCNF).
Analyze transaction processing concepts, ACID properties, concurrency control protocols, and recovery systems.
Evaluate indexing mechanisms (B+ trees, hashing), query optimization, and modern NoSQL architectures.

units.title: Introduction & Entity-Relationship Modeling
topics: Database System Concepts and Architecture
Data Models and Schemas
Three-Schema Architecture and Data Independence
Entity-Relationship (ER) Model: Entities, Attributes, and Relationships
Extended ER (EER) Modeling: Specialization, Generalization, and Aggregation
Conversion of ER/EER Diagrams to Relational Tables

units.title: Relational Model, Relational Algebra & SQL
topics: Relational Model Constraints and Relational Database Schemas
Relational Algebra Operations: Selection, Projection, Cartesian Product, Join, and Division
Tuple Relational Calculus and Domain Relational Calculus
Data Definition Language (DDL) and Data Manipulation Language (DML) in SQL
Nested Queries, Correlated Subqueries, Aggregate Functions, and Grouping (GROUP BY, HAVING)
Triggers, Assertions, Views, and Security Authorizations

units.title: Database Design Theory & Normalization
topics: Informal Design Guidelines for Relation Schemas
Functional Dependencies and Inference Rules (Armstrong's Axioms)
Normal Forms: First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF), and Third Normal Form (3NF)
Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
Multi-valued Dependencies and Fourth Normal Form (4NF)
Lossless-Join Decomposition and Dependency Preservation

units.title: Transaction Processing & Concurrency Control
topics: Transaction Concepts, States, and ACID Properties
Concurrent Executions, Schedules, and Serializability (Conflict and View Serializability)
Concurrency Control: Two-Phase Locking (2PL) Protocol (Strict, Rigorous)
Timestamp Ordering and Multiversion Concurrency Control Protocols
Deadlock Handling: Prevention, Detection, and Recovery Strategies
Database Failure Types, Log-Based Recovery, and Checkpointing Algorithms

units.title: Storage, Indexing, Query Optimization & NoSQL
topics: File Organizations: Ordered vs Unordered Records, Hashing Techniques
Single-Level and Multi-Level Indexing: Primary, Clustering, and Secondary Indexes
B-Trees and B+ Tree Index Structures (Search, Insert, and Delete Algorithms)
Query Processing Steps and Cost-Based Query Optimization
Introduction to NoSQL Databases: Key-Value, Document, Column-Oriented, and Graph Databases
CAP Theorem and BASE Consistency Model

course_outcomes.description: Explain the architecture, system calls, and structure of modern operating systems.
Analyze CPU scheduling algorithms and process synchronization mechanisms.
Formulate deadlock prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and detection techniques.
Apply memory management techniques including paging, segmentation, and virtual memory page replacement.
Evaluate file systems, disk scheduling algorithms, and OS protection mechanisms.

units.title: OS Overview & Process Management
topics: Operating System Structures, Dual-Mode Operation, and System Calls
Process Concept, Process States, and Process Control Block (PCB)
Process Scheduling: Queues, Schedulers, and Context Switching
Inter-Process Communication (IPC): Shared Memory and Message Passing
Multithreading Models: User-Level and Kernel-Level Threads

units.title: CPU Scheduling & Process Synchronization
topics: CPU Scheduling Criteria: Turnaround Time, Waiting Time, and Response Time
Scheduling Algorithms: FCFS, SJF, Priority Scheduling, and Round Robin
The Critical Section Problem and Peterson's Algorithm Solution
Hardware Synchronization (TestAndSet, Swap) and Semaphores (Counting and Binary)
Classical Synchronization Problems: Producer-Consumer, Dining Philosophers, and Readers-Writers

units.title: Deadlocks & Resource Allocation
topics: System Model and Four Coffman Necessary Conditions for Deadlock
Resource-Allocation Graphs (RAG) and Cycle Detection
Deadlock Prevention and Elimination of Mutual Exclusion/Hold and Wait
Deadlock Avoidance: Banker's Algorithm for Safety and Resource Request
Deadlock Detection Algorithms and Recovery from Deadlock

units.title: Memory Management & Virtual Memory
topics: Logical vs Physical Address Space, Dynamic Loading, and Swapping
Contiguous Memory Allocation: First-Fit, Best-Fit, Worst-Fit, and Fragmentation
Non-Contiguous Allocation: Paging Mechanism, Page Table Structure, and TLB
Segmentation with Paging Architecture
Virtual Memory: Demand Paging and Page Fault Handling Routine
Page Replacement Algorithms: FIFO, Optimal (OPT), and Least Recently Used (LRU)
Thrashing, Working-Set Model, and Page-Fault Frequency

units.title: Storage Management & File Systems
topics: File Concepts, Access Methods, and Directory Structures (Single-level to Tree)
File System Mounting, Allocation Methods: Contiguous, Linked, and Indexed Allocation
Free Space Management: Bit Vectors and Linked Lists
Disk Structure and Disk Scheduling Algorithms: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, and LOOK
RAID Levels and Data Redundancy Strategies

course_outcomes.description: Determine asymptotic time and space complexities using Big-O, Omega, and Master Theorem.
Design efficient algorithms using Divide-and-Conquer paradigms.
Apply Greedy strategies and Dynamic Programming to optimization problems.
Formulate Backtracking and Branch-and-Bound algorithms for combinatorial challenges.
Classify computational complexity into P, NP, NP-Complete, and NP-Hard classes.

units.title: Algorithm Analysis & Recurrences
topics: Asymptotic Notations: Big-O, Big-Omega, Big-Theta, Little-o, and Little-omega
Worst-case, Average-case, and Best-case Analysis of Algorithms
Solving Recurrence Relations: Substitution Method and Recursion-Tree Method
Master Theorem for Divide-and-Conquer Recurrences
Amortized Analysis: Aggregate, Accounting, and Potential Methods

units.title: Divide and Conquer & Sorting Lower Bounds
topics: Divide-and-Conquer Design Strategy and Recurrence Formulation
Merge Sort and Quick Sort (Partitioning Analysis and Randomized Pivot)
Binary Search and Finding Min-Max Element Simultaneously
Strassen's Matrix Multiplication Algorithm
Lower Bounds for Comparison-Based Sorting (Decision Tree Model)

units.title: Greedy Method & Dynamic Programming
topics: Greedy Strategy Principles and Optimal Substructure Property
Fractional Knapsack Problem and Job Sequencing with Deadlines
Minimum Spanning Trees: Kruskal's (Union-Find) and Prim's Algorithms
Dijkstra's Single-Source Shortest Path Algorithm
Dynamic Programming Strategy: Memoization vs Tabulation
0/1 Knapsack Problem and Matrix Chain Multiplication
Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) and Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Path

units.title: Backtracking & Branch and Bound
topics: State Space Tree Representation and Depth-First Search Exploration
The N-Queens Problem (State Space Formulation and Pruning)
Sum of Subsets Problem and Graph Coloring Problem
Hamiltonian Cycles Problem
Branch and Bound Technique: FIFO, LIFO, and Least-Cost (LC) Search
Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) using Branch and Bound

units.title: Tractable & Intractable Problems (NP-Completeness)
topics: Deterministic vs Non-Deterministic Algorithms
Complexity Classes: P, NP, NP-Hard, and NP-Complete
Polynomial-Time Reductions and Proof Techniques
Cook-Levin Theorem and Satisfiability (SAT) Problem
Proving NP-Completeness for 3-SAT, Clique, Vertex Cover, and Subset-Sum
Approximation Algorithms for NP-Hard Problems (Vertex Cover & Metric TSP)

course_outcomes.description: Construct accessible, modern web interfaces using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
Develop dynamic server-side applications using RESTful web services and asynchronous APIs.
Implement client-server security protocols, authentication (JWT/OAuth), and session management.
Evaluate cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) and deployment architectures.
Design scalable microservices, containerization using Docker, and serverless workflows.

units.title: Frontend Architecture & Modern JavaScript
topics: HTML5 Semantic Elements and Document Object Model (DOM) Tree
CSS3 Flexbox, Grid Layouts, and Responsive Design Media Queries
JavaScript ES6+ Features: Promises, Async/Await, Destructuring, and Closures
Event Bubbling, Event Capturing, and Event Delegation
Client-Side Storage: LocalStorage, SessionStorage, and IndexedDB

units.title: Asynchronous Communication & RESTful APIs
topics: HTTP/HTTPS Protocols, Request/Response Headers, and Status Codes
AJAX, Fetch API, and XMLHttpRequest Architecture
REST Architectural Constraints and CRUD Endpoint Design
JSON Serialization and Schema Validation
WebSockets for Real-Time Bidirectional Communication

units.title: Web Security, Authentication & Session Handling
topics: State Management: Cookies, Sessions, and Stateless Tokens
JSON Web Tokens (JWT) Structure and Verification Flow
OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant Flow
Common Web Vulnerabilities: SQL Injection, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and CSRF
Content Security Policy (CSP) and Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)

units.title: Cloud Computing Fundamentals & Virtualization
topics: NIST Definition of Cloud Computing and Essential Characteristics
Cloud Service Models: IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS Architectures and Comparison
Cloud Deployment Models: Public, Private, Hybrid, and Multi-Cloud
Hardware Virtualization: Hypervisor Type-1 and Type-2 Architectures
Virtual Machine Migration and Resource Provisioning

units.title: Microservices, Containers & Serverless
topics: Monolithic vs Microservices Architecture Patterns
Containerization Principles: Linux Namespaces, Cgroups, and Docker Architecture
Dockerfile Creation, Image Layering, and Container Lifecycle
Introduction to Container Orchestration using Kubernetes
Serverless Computing and Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) Execution Model

course_outcomes.description: Formulate state-space search algorithms and heuristic evaluations for problem solving.
Apply supervised learning algorithms for regression and classification tasks.
Analyze unsupervised clustering, dimensionality reduction, and model evaluation metrics.
Construct neural network architectures and backpropagation learning models.
Evaluate reinforcement learning agents and generative AI ethical considerations.

units.title: Problem Formulation & Heuristic Search
topics: Agents and Environments, Rationality, and PEAS Descriptions
Uninformed Search Strategies: Breadth-First Search, Depth-First Search, and Uniform-Cost Search
Informed (Heuristic) Search: Greedy Best-First Search and A* Search Algorithm
Admissibility and Consistency of Heuristics
Adversarial Search: Minimax Algorithm and Alpha-Beta Pruning

units.title: Supervised Learning: Regression & Classification
topics: Supervised Learning Workflow: Feature Vectors, Training, and Testing Splits
Linear Regression: Cost Function, Ordinary Least Squares, and Gradient Descent
Logistic Regression for Binary and Multi-Class Classification
Decision Tree Induction: Information Gain, Entropy, and Gini Impurity
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Hyperplane, Maximum Margin, and Kernel Trick
Ensemble Methods: Random Forests and Gradient Boosting

units.title: Unsupervised Learning & Model Validation
topics: Clustering Paradigms: K-Means Algorithm, Elbow Method, and Silhouette Score
Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering and Dendrogram Analysis
Dimensionality Reduction: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Eigenvalues
Bias-Variance Tradeoff and Regularization (L1 Lasso, L2 Ridge)
Model Evaluation Metrics: Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC Curve, and Confusion Matrix
Cross-Validation Techniques (K-Fold, Stratified K-Fold)

units.title: Neural Networks & Deep Learning Foundations
topics: Biological vs Artificial Neuron: Perceptron Model and Activation Functions (Sigmoid, ReLU, Tanh, Softmax)
Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Architecture and Feedforward Propagation
Backpropagation Algorithm Derivation using Chain Rule of Calculus
Loss Functions: Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Cross-Entropy Loss
Optimization Algorithms: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), Momentum, and Adam Optimizer
Vanishing and Exploding Gradient Problems and Batch Normalization

units.title: Reinforcement Learning & AI Ethics
topics: Reinforcement Learning Elements: Agent, Environment, State, Action, and Reward
Markov Decision Processes (MDP) and Bellman Equations
Q-Learning Algorithm and Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma (Epsilon-Greedy)
Overview of Deep Q-Networks (DQN)
Fairness, Bias, Accountability, and Explainability in AI Models
Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Ethical Safety Challenges
